calls.head: Expect the Avalanche to have the puck more
calls.body: The Avalanche have been the league’s best at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Jets near the bottom. Expect the Avalanche to spend more of the night in the Jets’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

COL.head: We gave Colorado a 63% chance, but Winnipeg had other ideas.

surprises.head: Colorado’s kill smothered Winnipeg’s power play
surprises.body: Colorado has one of the league’s stingiest penalty kills. Even by those standards, this was a dry night: Winnipeg’s power play created 1.4 expected goals per 60, against their usual 7.9 (about 7.0 against Colorado) and a league average of 7.7. A team strays this far about once every 45 games.

story.head: Connor scores with a minute left to lift the Jets
paras: The Jets’ Josh Morrissey left early in the second period and didn’t return. Two days later, he was listed as day to day with an upper-body injury. Jaden Schwartz scored his first goal for Colorado early in the period to open the scoring, but Kyle Connor tied it 1-1 for Winnipeg just over a minute later. Cole Perfetti put the Jets ahead 2-1 late in the period. Fedor Svechkov scored his first goal for Colorado with less than eight minutes left to tie it 2-2, but that was the last goal the Avalanche would get. Connor struck again with a minute left to put the Jets ahead for good.

The Avalanche outshot the Jets 34-19, but the Jets’ looks were better, so the chances came out about even. The Avs hit two posts and still lost. Stuart Skinner made 32 saves for the Jets, and Mackenzie Blackwood stopped 16 of 19 at the other end. The Jets improved to 3-0-1, tied for first in the NHL in points percentage, while the Avalanche fell to 2-1-0, giving up the best points percentage in the NHL to the Jets.

items.text: Kyle Connor tied Ilya Kovalchuk for third on the Jets’ all-time goals list, with 328.
Three straight wins for the Jets.
Cole Perfetti has a point in every game this season, with a goal in each of the last three.
The Avalanche’s Zachary L'Heureux played his first game of the season, after missing the first two.
